{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Florida Gas Transmission Pipeline''' is a natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2smVBv2 Florida Gas Transmission Pipeline], A Barrel Full, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

==Location==

=== System location ===
The pipeline runs from Port Lavaca, Texas, to Miami, Florida.<ref name=source2>[http://fgttransfer.energytransfer.com/ipost/FGT/maps/system-map "Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC,] Energy Transfer, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref> The route below has been adapted from the EIA database.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php|title=Layer Information for Interactive State Maps|website=www.eia.gov|access-date=2021-11-09}}</ref>

==Background==

=== System background ===
The Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) pipeline is an approximately 5,300-mile system<ref name=kinder/> that transports natural gas from south Texas to south Florida. FGT is owned by Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC, a 100% owned subsidiary of Citrus Corp. Citrus Corp is a 50/50 joint venture between Kinder Morgan, Inc. (NYSE: KMI) and Energy Transfer Partners. <ref name=kinder>[https://www.kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT/default.aspx Florida Gas Transmission], Kinder Morgan, accessed Aug. 27, 2021.</ref> It is supplied by the Destin Gas Pipeline and there is an interconnection with Gulf South Gas Pipeline System and the Southern Natural Gas Pipeline Company at Clay County, Florida. <ref name=source1/>

=== Western Division Project ===
The expansion project would add miles to the Alabama and Mississippi section of the pipeline.<ref name="ft" /> Construction was completed and the project became operational in 2018.<ref name="eia0421" />

=== East-West Project ===
East West Pipeline is an operating extension of the Florida Gas Transmission pipeline in Texas and Louisiana.<ref name="source12">[https://s3.amazonaws.com/pgj-wp-media/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/PN1018-Planned-Projects.pdf Planned Projects], Pipeline News, accessed October 2018</ref> The pipeline runs through Matagorda and Wharton counties, Texas to Acadia Parish, Louisiana, USA.

On August 16, 2018, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) approved construction of a part of the East West Pipeline along the Texas coast.<ref name="source22">[https://texasenergyreport.com/blog/2018/08/15/13574/ Partial Construction On East-West Pipeline Expansion Granted], Texas Energy Report, August 16, 2018</ref> It would transport natural gas from two proposed receipt points and one existing receipt point in Louisiana to two proposed delivery points on Florida Gas’s existing pipeline system in the Gulf Coast region of Texas.<ref name="source1" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the construction of the project was completed in January 2019 and began service.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php|title=Natural Gas Data - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)|website=www.eia.gov|access-date=2023-08-08}}</ref>
=== Galveston County Project ===
The project would install two pipeline segments along the FGT Mainline that would connect to a natural gas power plant in Galveston, Texas.<ref name="eia0421" /> As of April 2021, the Energy Information Administration (EIA) had the project listed as complete.<ref name="eia0421" /> The project was completed in February 2021.<ref name="eia0421" />

=== Putnam Expansion Project ===
The expansion project would be expected to deliver natural gas to the 1,183 MW Seminole Electric Cooperative power unit. The additional capacity would be entirely in Florida.<ref name="eia" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project was under construction.<ref name="eia0421" /> As of February 2022, construction was complete and the project was presumed to be operational.<ref name="eia0421" />
=== East Louisiana Project ===
The expansion was planned to add a new delivery point to Entergy Louisiana in Louisiana, allowing bidirectional flow on mainline.<ref name="eia" /> The U.S. Energy Information Agency reported that the project was completed on April 7, 2020.<ref name="eianov" />
===Big Bend Project===
The project involved a loop extension in Calhoun and Jefferson Counties, Florida that would serve Tampa Electric Company’s Peoples Gas System.<ref name="eia0421" />

According to the EIA, the project was cancelled as of March 2022.<ref name="eia0421" />
